statement.p: An airplane is flying toward the southwest. Consider the wind velocity vectors \vec w_1 = 3\mathit{\vec i}-\mathit{\vec j} \qquad \vec w_2 = -\mathit{\vec i}-3\mathit{\vec j} \qquad \vec w_3 = \mathit{\vec i}+6\mathit{\vec j} \vec w_4 = -8\mathit{\vec i}+2\mathit{\vec j} \qquad \vec w_5 = -4\mathit{\vec i}-\mathit{\vec j}.
Which of the wind velocity vectors increases the plane's speed the most?

Wind
?
w1
w2
w3
w4
w5
Which slows down the plane the most?

Wind

w2

static.solution:
\vec w in the direction of the airplane. A direction vector for the airplane is \vec v = -\mathit{\vec i}-\mathit{\vec j}. The component of \vec w_1 in the direction of \vec v is given by {{\vec w_1 \cdot \vec v} \over ||{\vec v}}|| = {-2 \over \sqrt{2}} \approx -1.41.
Similarly, we find the component for each wind vector in the direction of the airplane. We see that, in the direction of the airplane, the component of \vec w_1 is -1.41, of \vec w_2 is 2.83, of \vec w_3 is -4.95, of \vec w_4 is 4.24, and of \vec w_5 is 3.54.
Thus, the vector \vec w_4 increases the plane's speed the most and the vector \vec w_3 slows the plane down the most.
